steps: Replica A updates its local CRDT without coordination.
Replica B concurrently performs another valid update.
Replicas exchange states or commutative operations.
Associative, commutative, idempotent merge makes both converge on the same value.

lesson.scenario: Two replicas implement an observed-remove set where unique add tags and tombstones merge by set union.
entities: Stores element-tag pairs created or learned by A
Stores tags A has observed and removed
Stores element-tag pairs created or learned by B
Stores tags B has observed and removed
Shows an element when any add tag lacks a tombstone

steps.title: A adds milk with a unique tag
steps.narration: A creates tag a1, so milk is present because a1 is not tombstoned.
steps.outcome: The add is locally visible without coordinating with B.
steps.invariant: Every add uses a globally unique tag so concurrent instances remain distinguishable.

steps.title: B concurrently adds the same element
steps.narration: B has not seen a1 and independently creates tag b1 for milk.
steps.outcome: Both replicas contain milk through different causal adds.
steps.invariant: Concurrent adds do not overwrite or deduplicate each other’s tags.

steps.title: A removes only what it observed
steps.narration: A removes milk by tombstoning its known tag a1; it cannot remove unseen b1.
action: remove milk: tombstone observed tag a1
steps.outcome: A’s local view is empty while B’s concurrent add remains live.
steps.invariant: Remove records exactly the add tags visible in its causal context.

steps.title: Union merge preserves concurrent add
steps.narration: The replicas union add-sets and tombstones: adds become {a1,b1}, removes contain only a1.
action: union adds and tombstones at both replicas
steps.outcome: Milk remains present because concurrent tag b1 was not observed by A’s remove.
steps.invariant: Merge is associative, commutative, and idempotent set union.

steps.title: B removes the now-observed live tag
steps.narration: After convergence B removes milk and tombstones b1 in addition to retained a1.
action: remove milk: tombstone live tag b1
steps.outcome: B can remove the concurrent add only after observing its tag.
steps.invariant: A remove cannot erase an add outside the remover’s observed context.

steps.title: Tombstone merge converges to empty
steps.narration: Unioning B’s tombstones gives both replicas removes {a1,b1}; no live add tag remains.
steps.outcome: Both replicas deterministically materialize the empty set.
steps.invariant: Tombstones require causal garbage collection; deleting them before all replicas observe them can resurrect removed tags.

production.scenario: A live sports watch-party service stores room reactions in a CRDT so viewers in different regions can keep tapping emoji during a regional partition and still converge on one final count.
components: Tap heart and fire reactions during a live playoff stream
Accepts reactions from viewers connected to the east region
Accepts reactions from viewers connected to the west region
Merges reaction adds and removals without a single synchronous writer
Broadcasts converged room totals back to viewers
Admin control for removing abusive reactions and blocked users from the room state
flows: tap fire emoji in room finals-2026
Viewers in the east region keep sending reactions every few seconds during the game.
The east gateway records the local reaction into the CRDT state without coordinating with the west region first.
If the west region reconnects after a partition, its queued reactions still merge into the same room state.
Moderation actions become CRDT updates too, so deletes converge with late adds instead of fighting them.
The service periodically writes the merged room state as the durable view that restart recovery will read.
The fanout stream picks up the converged totals from the persisted room state.
After any reconnect, every phone sees the same final reaction counts even if local updates were accepted in different regions.
